C graph uses flat edges and a handwritten map; Dewy uses per-node arrays and an insertion-ordered map.
String equality uses separately allocated payloads; C uses pointer/length pairs and libc memcmp, Dewy uses runtime strings.
Kernel times exclude input generation; wall times include the complete process.
Thread CPU timing excludes descheduling, but CPU frequency and cache contention still matter.

measurement_notes: All initial and focused matched samples are retained. Follow-up measurements cover only the unresolved Netpong and Dunes compilation comparisons.
All eight runtime workloads match accepted artifacts in both modes. Fresh boundary and full-size checks still run; runtime timing and fresh C ratios are unmeasured for this stage.
The seeded prototype instruction-count reduction is diagnostic, not elapsed-time acceptance evidence. The accepted compiler was independently bootstrapped from C.

The prototype pilot retained completed compilation samples but its runtime-certificate assertion failed: the artifact certificate declined equivalence across different temporary input-directory layouts and safely fell back to fresh runtime timing. Those discarded runtime samples are not used for acceptance. The final stage uses the normal temporary-directory layout and all eight certificates pass.

The host is contended; the roughly 0.3% default / 0.8% release paired compilation gain is small. The structural improvement removes repeated per-parameter body traversal, not a claim of achieving the overall throughput target.
